points.text: The PR stamps the entry: `verified: by process:pilot-dev` and `pilot.verifiedCommit: 7c1d9e0`. A PR never stamps an entry, because only a lint run writes the stamp after finding the entry conforming. Clear it with `python3 .pilot/pilot.py wiki set names-only --clear-stamp` so `verified` and `verifiedCommit` are empty. Keep the move from `specified` to `implemented`. That move is correct, since this PR completes the entry and the test replay below shows the code satisfies both of its statements. The commit named in the stamp also gives no assurance, because it is not the PR head. I did not review the stamped commit itself.

The order of the names is not covered. `test_prints_only_names` sorts the lines before comparing them, so it cannot tell whether `--names-only` keeps the search order (farthest first today) or changes it. The entry only says "one place name per line" and that the output is otherwise unchanged. Make the test assert the order and state it in the entry, so the behavior is specified and tested. The expected order is the same as the default output, i.e. `Cafe du Pont` then `Cafe Lumiere`. Do not change the sort itself in this PR.
